title: SRE weekly pocket journal - 2029-07-22
content:
Week pocket journal (raw notes) - context: quick capture for rotation handoff and async readers

Date range: 2029-07-15 -> 2029-07-22
Owner / recorder: Ava Patel (SRE rotation lead this week)
Collaborators in flight: Marcus Li (serving runtime), Sofia Romero (observability), Ethan Clarke (platform eng)

Top-line summary:
- Relatively steady week after Tuesday night incident (short model-serving plateau). No customer-facing SLA breaches.
- Error budget for inference-read endpoints consumed ~2.1% this week (out of monthly 5%). Watch for compounding during next week's canaries.
- On-call fatigue signal: 3 consecutive pages for same subsystem in 48h -> tweak alert noise.

SLO & metrics snapshot (quick numbers, approximate):
- Inference p50/p95/p99: 85ms / 220ms / 890ms (global median across hosted API regions)
- Embeddings p95: 420ms
- 5xx rate (inference): 0.18% daily average, spike to 0.9% during incident window
- Error budget remaining (monthly): ~2.9%
- Token throughput: 120M tokens/day (peak Tue 03:00 UTC 8.6k tok/s)

Major incident (brief chronology) - Tue 2029-07-16 02:58 UTC
- Symptom: Surge of 5xx from model-serving hosts in us-west region, correlated with sudden drop in available model cache memory and OOM kills on older GPU hosts.
- Pager events: automatic escalations to on-call SRE -> platform (Marcus) -> serving runtime (Ethan).
- Mitigations applied within 11m: trimmed new schedule for background compaction job, rolled back an aggressive auto-eviction experiment from last deploy, scaled up warm pools ( +12 nodes) to buy runway.
- Root cause hypothesis: regression in blob-store compaction combined with kernel-level mem reclaim behavior on older driver stack (NVIDIA 525.x); compaction increased resident set for a subset of process trees, pushing older nodes past OOM threshold.
- Short-term follow-ups: pin compaction window to off-peak, increase eviction headroom, add guardrails to compaction job (SRE-1873).
- Long-term action: add a canary that runs compaction in a fenced namespace for 72h before enabling cluster-wide; upgrade affected hosts to driver 530.x during maintenance window (owner: Ethan, due 2029-08-05).

Alerting & runbook notes:
- False-positive noise from inference-cache-miss alert (firing threshold too tight). Proposal: change to p99 > 600ms + sustained 2m window before page. Owner: Sofia. Target: 2029-07-28.
- Runbook fragment updated: model-serving-oom.md (added checklist to escalate to kernel-driver-owner and commands to collect per-process cgroups snapshot). See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/542

On-call handoff (for next rotation) - items to call out:
- Current open tickets: SRE-1873 (compaction gating), SRE-1890 (pager noise investigation), PLAT-940 (host driver upgrade schedule).
- Escalation path reminder: first escalation -> platform #oncall-platform, second -> eng-leads (pager escalations via ops pager).
- Temporary mitigations in place that must be reverted once root cause long-term fixes land: increased warm pool (manual), compaction scheduler disabled for non-fenced namespaces. Note: remember to remove manual warm pool by 2029-08-07 if not auto-scaling back.

Operational experiments & notes:
- A/B test: lowered batch_coalesce window from 40ms->25ms for latency-sensitive serving (canary 10% traffic). Early signal: p95 down 15ms, tail unaffected. Continue through next week's traffic wedge.
- Observability tweak: added a dedicated tracing tag for 'compaction-phase' to correlate CPU/GPU memory retention during maintenance jobs.

Action items (owners & short deadlines):
- Ethan: schedule driver upgrade window for affected sku (ETA 2029-08-05).
- Marcus: implement fenced compaction canary and run for 72h (ETA 2029-07-30).
- Sofia: tune missing-cache alert (change to p99 + 2m sustained) and backfill pager threshold tests (ETA 2029-07-28).
- Ava: run a short post-incident retro w/notes + share with customers team if EBD used (ETA 2029-07-25).

Runbook / playbook items modified this week:
- model-serving-oom.md: added collection commands, escalation steps, immediate mitigations, owners.
- alert-routing.md: added a new route rule to suppress non-urgent cache misses during compaction windows.

Meeting notes (SLO sync, Thu 2029-07-18)
Attendees: Ava, Sofia, Marcus, Priya (product), Daniel (customer success)
- SLO runway looks OK but product asked for a tighter latency SLA for high-tier customers. Conversation: propose a dedicated capacity offering (Dedicated pools) with isolated warm pools and guaranteed tail SLOs. Action: Priya to scope product proposal; SRE to provide cost model.
- Agreed start: draft cost delta per 10k qps on dedicated pool by next Thu (2029-07-25).

Notes to self / raw scraps (keep)
- If driver upgrade is scheduled, run a small canary on driver 530.x in staging overlay before rolling to us-west.
- Check with infra team about retirement schedule for older hosts (list: gpu-sku-7a, gpu-sku-9b).
- Confirm whether auto-eviction experiment was rolled out to eu-west as well (I saw a single deploy but need confirmation).

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Should we broaden compaction gated canary to all maintenance jobs or keep it specific to blob-store compaction? (tradeoff speed of rollout vs blast radius)
- What's acceptable error budget burn ceiling before product intervention? Current informal threshold is 4% / month; need to document formally.

Next week's focus (short):
- Close SRE-1873 (compaction gating) and run post-fix stress tests.
- Finalize driver upgrade plan and run canary.
- Tune alerts and reduce pager noise; measure pager_count per engineer next rotation.
- Start drafting Dedicated pool tail-SLO cost model with product.

Appendix (links / refs):
- Incident ticket: SRE-1869
- Follow-up / patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/542
- Confluence SLO dashboard: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Dashboard
- Pager history snapshot: (internal) slack thread #ops-incident-2029-07-16

Quick checklist for incoming on-call:
- Read this doc (pocket journal) + incident SRE-1869 notes
- Ensure warm pool autoscale is healthy (goal: at least 6 warm nodes per region)
- Verify compaction scheduler is in fenced mode (if not, call Marcus)

End of pocket capture. This is intentionally informal — will distill to a cleaner weekly digest if requested by ops manager.
